title: metadata-protocol: the layered read of a doc name two enabled packages hold answers one holder's layers while the plain read refuses (ADR-0150 D3/D5)
body:
domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTkZnXtRhuEiiyidvJ

Filing gate: class (a). Two doors disagree on the same address. Raised as should-fix S3 by contract-review record 6903815196 (review#2) on PR #33885, at head a2b29893.
Prior rulings read: ADR-0150 D3/D5 (a name two holders hold is refused with candidates, never answered by picking one); PR #34036 (merged 2026-11-15, "a bare doc read refuses a name two enabled packages hold, naming both"); PR #33885 (the layered read answers as the plain read for the types the registry reads by package). Dedupe: searched `layered doc readsByPackage` and `getMetaItemLayered doc two packages`; the only hit is #32622 itself (package-read types, no `doc`).

## What happens (read on the tree, not measured)
- Since #34036, the plain read of a `doc` name that two enabled packages hold refuses with 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and names both.
- The layered read's guard in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` is `readsByPackage(type)`. `doc` is not in that set, so `getMetaItemLayered({ type: 'doc', name })` never reaches the judgment and answers one holder's layers.
- REST `/layers` answers the 409 only where a step of its chain asks the plain read. The composition with no engine wired was not followed.
- When the doc refusal is thrown inside the REST `/layers` route, #33885's catch now gives it candidates too. That path is not pinned.
- Neither PR opened the gap on its own. It appears where the two meet.

## Expected
- The layered read asks the doc judgment before it reads layers, as the plain read does. A bare `/layers` (and `?layers=true`) of a `doc` name two enabled packages hold answers 409 with `details.candidates` naming both, in process and on both transports. `?package=` of each holder still serves that holder's layers. CONTROL: a doc name one package holds is served.
- Measure first. If the REST or dispatcher door already refuses in every composition, the card reduces to pins.

Clause-② arm: `yes (narrowing)` if a served layered answer becomes refused. `Metadata-protocol: none`.
